authority_statement: Informational report only; the deterministic LFighter pipeline retains all security decision authority.
executive_summary: In development and validation evidence, the plain DDoS-to-Benign prediction rate exceeded the paired clean rate, while the defended rate was lower than the plain rate. Reconstruction reduced attribution distance toward the paired preattack clean reference, not an oracle clean state.

facts.statement: The plain attack mean DDoS-to-Benign prediction rate was 0.613848, versus 0.056499 in the paired clean branch.
The defended mean DDoS-to-Benign prediction rate was 0.121137, an absolute reduction of 0.492711 from the plain attack branch.
Mean and minimum malicious recall were 1.000000; maximum benign false-positive rate was 0.100000.
Normalized attribution distance decreased from 0.652957 to 0.495206, with recovery fraction 0.241595.

interpretations.statement: Observed prediction behavior is consistent with targeted suppression of DDoS predictions toward the Benign class; it does not establish malicious intent.
Reconstruction moved the attribution profile toward its paired preattack clean reference; this is not evidence of oracle clean restoration.

refusals: Refused: malicious intent is unsupported by the evidence.
Refused: oracle clean recovery is unsupported; oracle-clean attribution state was unavailable.
uncertainties: The clean attribution comparator is the paired round 4 preattack reference, not an oracle clean state.
Rejected and oracle-clean attribution states were unavailable and were not substituted.
Per-client detector scores and numeric thresholds were not materialized.
Evidence is limited to development and validation; reserved test arrays remained closed.
